correctness.rationale: Largest-prime-factor decomposition bounds the cofactor and repeated highest-prime power for positive fixed thresholds, including strict-boundary cases. A prime-divisor expansion controls the first moment; small higher powers, excluded primes dividing the complementary factor and the large-cofactor tail are summably negligible. Multiplicativity yields the Euler product and boundedness 0<R<=2 transfers the first-moment asymptotic to every fixed integral moment. Exact finite verification at six thresholds is supplementary, not a substitute.

value.rationale: The originating 2025 sign inequality naturally prompts study of its dimensionless deficiency. A later 2026 primary preprint explicitly asks for this normalized distribution. The theorem supplies a complete first-order exceptional tail for every fixed t, including discontinuity boundaries, and a full set of exact logarithmic moment constants. This characterizes how and how often the normalized deficiency deviates from one, beyond a routine equality-case classification.
